research_question: Is the structural similarity between the author's early and later concepts evidence of internal intellectual continuity?

primary_hypothesis.statement: The observed structural overlap reflects internal continuity in the author's problem development.
primary_hypothesis.failure_effect: The continuity claim in the center conclusion must be retracted.

predictions.expected_observation: The later text explicitly reuses the earlier problem vocabulary with the same function.

rival_hypotheses.statement: Both texts draw independently on a shared conceptual resource available in the period.
rival_hypotheses.simplicity_note: Fewer assumptions when no direct authorial linkage is documented.

predictions.expected_observation: The same vocabulary appears in unrelated contemporaneous authors.
Neither text cites the other's distinctive source.

rival_hypotheses.statement: The similarity is an artifact of an overly broad analytical template.
rival_hypotheses.simplicity_note: Requires no biographical assumption but must show the template generates false positives.

predictions.expected_observation: Applying the same template to random unrelated pairs produces equal similarity scores.
At least one unrelated pair passes the primary criteria.

falsification_conditions.statement: If no source from the author's early phase contains the later problem vocabulary, H1 fails.
If the vocabulary is fully explained by the shared source, H1 is not preferred.

operational_criteria.statement: Object typology: the two texts address the same type of object.
operational_criteria.inclusion_test: Both texts describe a structured whole that is external to the individual.
operational_criteria.exclusion_test: Parallel terms about different objects do not count.

operational_criteria.statement: Mediation typology: the same mediating structure is at work.
operational_criteria.inclusion_test: Both texts use the same mediating category in the same functional slot.
operational_criteria.exclusion_test: A mediating term present in only one text is insufficient.

operational_criteria.statement: Problem polarity: the same problem polarity appears.
operational_criteria.inclusion_test: Both texts frame the same tension between the individual and the objective world.
operational_criteria.exclusion_test: Similar polarity in one text only is not counted.

operational_criteria.statement: Pathological structure: the same failure structure is diagnosed.
operational_criteria.inclusion_test: Both texts identify the same kind of pathological closure.
operational_criteria.exclusion_test: Different failure mechanisms are not counted.

operational_criteria.statement: Resolution direction: the same direction of resolution is proposed.
operational_criteria.inclusion_test: Both texts resolve the tension in the same direction.
operational_criteria.exclusion_test: Opposite resolution directions count against correspondence.

operational_criteria.statement: Diachronic connection: a temporal link is documented.
operational_criteria.inclusion_test: A dated source connects the early and late phases.
operational_criteria.exclusion_test: Untested chronological adjacency is not evidence.

diachronic_connection_evidence.observation: The early text contains the same problem vocabulary used in the later text.
The later text reuses the vocabulary without marking it as new.

negative_controls.reason_for_control: A contemporaneous text by the same author should not show the target structure.
negative_controls.expected_result: The control text fails the primary criteria.

negative_controls.reason_for_control: A contemporaneous author using the shared vocabulary should not reproduce the full structure.
negative_controls.expected_result: The control text fails the primary criteria.

rival_supported.conclusion_effect: The continuity claim is retracted and only shared-resource use is reported.

template_supported.conclusion_effect: The overlap is reported as a typological artifact only.

inconclusive.conclusion_effect: Only the typological correspondence is kept, with no continuity claim.
